## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. God heard her  (`#god-heard-her`)

Cited ayat: 58:1-2

> **58:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قَدْ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوْلَ ٱلَّتِى تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِى زَوْجِهَا وَتَشْتَكِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌۢ بَصِيرٌ
>
> **58:2** ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمْ إِنْ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمْ إِلَّا ٱلَّٰٓـِٔى وَلَدْنَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرًا مِّنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ وَزُورًا وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ

### Claims

**c1** (58:1): God has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God.

**c2** (58:1): God hears the exchange that took place, for God is hearing and seeing.

**c3** (58:2): Of those among them who make this declaration about their wives, God says that the wives are not their mothers, that their mothers are only those who bore them, and that they say an objectionable word and a falsehood.

**c4** (58:2): God is pardoning and forgiving.

### One-minute summary

God says that He has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God [c1]. God hears the exchange, and is hearing and seeing [c2]. Of those who make this declaration about their wives, He says that the wives are not their mothers [c3], and that God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].

### Complete story

God has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God [c1]. God hears the exchange that took place, for God is hearing and seeing [c2].

Of those among them who make this declaration about their wives, God says that the wives are not their mothers, that their mothers are only those who bore them, and that they say an objectionable word and a falsehood [c3]. God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].

### Deep study

The first verse says what God has heard and that He is hearing and seeing [c1][c2]. The woman is not named and her words are not given [c1]. The verse at 58:2 speaks of a declaration by men about their wives, and names it by the Arabic verb yuzahirun; the verse does not spell out the words of the declaration [c3]. It ends with God's names pardoning and forgiving [c4].

### Kids mode

God says that He has heard the woman who disputes about her husband and complains to Him [c1]. God hears and sees everything that is said [c2]. God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage begins with God hearing a complaint made to Him [c1][c2]. Another is that it calls an objectionable word an objectionable word, and ends with pardon and forgiveness [c3][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the woman is, who her husband is, what she said, or when and where it happened. The verse says 'the woman who disputes' and names no one.
- Not established: who the one addressed is. The verse says 'you' and does not name him.
- Not established: what the declaration of 58:2 consisted of in words. The verb is yuzahirun and the verse does not spell it out.
- This chapter does not restate 58:3-4, which set out what follows for those who make the declaration. They are left to a scholar to present or not, in the verses' own words; the draft states no judgement on them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the woman, of her husband, and the occasion. None is used in the story texts.
